strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy accuracy regression in Cauchy distribution where cauchy.pdf(1e200) emits a spurious overflow warning and cauchy.logpdf overflows/returns -inf for very large |x|. The reproduction targets the added tests in scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py (TestCauchy.test_pdf_no_overflow_warning and TestCauchy.test_logpdf).

pinned_because: The evidence names float64 behavior and uses np.finfo(np.float64).max for the overflow threshold; using the default NumPy float64 implementation consistently helps ensure the same threshold/regime. Pinning exact NumPy is optional but recommended if your CI uses a reproducible matrix.

strategy.test_command: source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py -k "TestCauchy and (test_pdf_no_overflow_warning or test_logpdf)"
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy SciPy revision 49e8876de1fb, running the test_command fails: (1) test_pdf_no_overflow_warning fails because stats.cauchy.pdf(1e200) triggers an overflow warning (i.e., PyTest sees the warning as a failure per SciPy's warnings configuration), and/or (2) test_logpdf fails because stats.cauchy.logpdf([x, -x]) returns -inf/incorrect values for large x such as 1e200 (and/or for _XMAX). On the fixed SciPy revision (the PR that contains the Cauchy fix merged after PR #21347), the same test_command passes: no overflow warning for pdf(1e200) and logpdf matches the provided reference values with rtol=1e-15.
strategy.numerical_probe: Use only the project’s own tests as the oracle: cauchy.pdf(1e200) (expects exact p==0.0 with no overflow warning) and cauchy.logpdf([x, -x]) at the parametrized points including 1e200 and _XMAX.

input_output_examples.expected_output: 0.0 (test asserts p == 0.0; additionally must not emit overflow warnings)

risks: The evidence does not specify the Python or NumPy versions; exact warning behavior can vary with NumPy/SciPy build options. If the warning-assertion behavior does not reproduce, adjust to the same major/minor NumPy version used in the failing report/CI.
The evidence does not specify the exact fixed commit; you must check out the PR #21347 fixed revision (merge commit or post-fix commit) rather than only relying on PR number.
The defect may be sensitive to float dtype. The evidence explicitly references float64 via np.finfo(np.float64).max; ensure the test runs with default float64 (avoid float32-only builds).

If SciPy’s test runner is configured to treat warnings strictly, the failure will surface as an assertion failure; if warnings are not treated strictly in your local setup, you might observe a warning without a failing assertion. In that case, reproduce using SciPy’s standard test invocation/flags used in CI.
Architecture/toolchain could matter for floating exception behavior; the evidence does not state platform constraints. Use a typical x86_64 Linux build unless your project CI indicates otherwise.

oracle.reference_source: Project test suite: TestCauchy.test_pdf_no_overflow_warning asserts p == 0.0 and expects no overflow warnings; TestCauchy.test_logpdf asserts_allclose(logp, [ref, ref], rtol=1e-15) with explicit ref constants (mpmath-derived) including -1.1447298858494002 for x=0.0 and -922.1787670834676 for x=1e200 and others.
oracle.why: The tests define the acceptance criteria directly: exact equality for pdf(1e200) and reference-based rtol=1e-15 for logpdf across multiple magnitudes, including very large values.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: Running the test_command on SciPy at commit 49e8876de1fb fails because `stats.cauchy.pdf(1e200)` raises a spurious overflow warning (the test suite treats this as a failure under SciPy’s warnings configuration) and/or because `stats.cauchy.logpdf([x, -x])` returns -inf/incorrect values for large |x| such as x=1e200 and the _XMAX case that extends beyond the float64 overflow-to-inf boundary for x^2.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: Running the same test_command on the fixed revision from PR #21347 passes: no overflow warning for pdf(1e200), pdf returns 0.0, and logpdf matches the provided mpmath-derived reference values (including finite results at 1e200 and _XMAX) within rtol=1e-15.
